The Market Basket Measure (MBM) and the Low-income Measure (LIM) are two different measures of poverty used in Canada. While they both aim to capture different aspects of economic well-being, they differ in their approach and thresholds. 

The LIM is based on after-tax income and is calculated as 50% of the median after-tax income of all individuals living in private households. This measure is often used as a general indicator of low-income status.

The MBM, on the other hand, is a more comprehensive measure that takes into account both income and expenses. It is designed to capture the costs of a specific basket of goods and services that are considered necessary for a basic standard of living. The MBM is typically updated every few years to reflect changes in the cost of living and the composition of the basket.
